title: How I program my Bench days for Natural Hypertrophy
summary: His two bench days, which are really chest/shoulders/triceps days. Day 1 has slingshot touch-and-go bench, paused bench and a waved 6-set overhead press supersetted with lots of chin-ups, then band, calf, neck and ab work. Day 2 is higher volume: slingshot bench, Spoto press, close-grip bench with Bradford presses and skull crushers (over 100 bench reps), then ring work and light side raises. The sessions take 2-3 hours.

claims.claim: A 'bench day' for a bodybuilder means most exercises are bench variations, chosen to target chest, shoulders and triceps.
His first bench day opens with touch-and-go Slingshot bench for 1-3 heavy sets of 4-8 reps; raw touch-and-go kills his shoulders, but he wants heavy weight and the unmatched stretch at the bottom.
He follows with paused bench without a Slingshot for 3 heavy sets of 4-8: it works the chest more, and the pause keeps him tight, prevents shoulder overextension and causes zero rotator cuff pain.
He supersets paused bench with dragon flags for abs and band work he calls 'strength restoration'.
Bench volume on day 1 is kept low so his shoulders stay fresh for the overhead press, his second strength movement of the day.
He waves overhead press over 6 heavy sets: a heavy warm-up at 135x5, up to his max (155 for 4-5), back down to 135, up to 155 again, and so on, always finishing on max reps at the top weight.
Presses need a lot of volume and frequency to grow, especially the overhead press, which is very hard to get stronger on; a stronger press means stronger and bigger shoulders.
He supersets overhead press with close-grip chin-ups (4-10 reps, not counted) on every warm-up and working set, totaling 60-100 chin-ups per session.
Chin-ups after presses balance the pressing for shoulder health and train his lats, a weak point; the back recovers from a lot, and calisthenics aren't taxing.

If he has energy left on day 1 he does a giant set of band work, chin-ups, push-ups, side raises and band front raises, then band curls for biceps tendon health, neck training, very high-volume calves and abs.
Day 1 is the lower-volume bench day with the least chest emphasis because of the overhead press.
After bench day 1 come three days of other sessions; the next upper day is biceps-focused with no horizontal pushing.
Slingshot bench warms him up for the pattern: after sets in the high 200s to 300 lbs with the Slingshot, 225 paused feels like nothing, whereas starting with paused bench feels off on his shoulders.
On day 2 he does Spoto press for 4 sets up to 12 reps, chasing the pump, supersetted with skull crushers (long head), dragon flags and band work.
He then does 4 rounds of close-grip bench for 10, Bradford press for 15 and skull crushers for 12.
The Bradford press is a behind-the-neck press alternated with a front overhead press.
By the end of bench day 2 he has done more than 100 reps with medium-to-heavy weight on bench variations.
Bench day 2 finishes with ring pull-ups and push-ups, light high-volume side raises (shoulders are fresh with no heavy overhead press), a push-up/pull-up superset, band work, neck, calves and abs.
Depending on the cycle he benches once or twice a week, and he makes his best progress with this setup, which lets him control intensity and volume.
Bench day 1 takes him 2-2.5 hours; bench day 2 takes about 3 hours.

exercises.name: Slingshot bench press (touch-and-go)
cues: touch and go for the bottom stretch
exercises.why: heavy chest work and stretch without shoulder pain; warms up the pattern

exercises.name: Paused bench press
cues: pause keeps you tight and stops shoulder overextension
exercises.why: more chest work, no rotator cuff pain

exercises.name: Overhead press
cues: wave between warm-up weight and max for 6 sets
finish on max reps at top weight

exercises.name: Light side raises
exercises.why: side delts are fresh with no heavy overhead press
